ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI booking (F8: $61.32, distance component $43.64 over 30.95 km), so diversion mileage enters the fare and RD-2's mileage-unit refund is the only refund mechanism here [F8][RD-2]. GPS records two off-route segments, F3 (18:46–18:56, +5.66 km) and F4 (19:03–19:12, +4.78 km), each tested separately against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F3][F4][RD-1].

F4 is settled: the rider's last message is timestamped 18:43, twenty minutes before F4 started at 19:03, and the complete timestamped chat record contains no rider message authorising any route change after that [F10][F11][F4]. The driver's post-trip statement "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" is a driver claim, not the rider's own pre-segment message, so it is not consent (G11) [F12][F4][RD-5]. No RD-4 exemption applies: only speed band 4 on BKE/PIE and no incidents near the route, so RD-4(a) is unmet and band evidence cannot exempt alone [F13][F14][F15][RD-4]. F4 therefore counts under RD-2 [F4][RD-2]. No stop is involved, so RD-3 does not apply to either segment [F3][F4][RD-3].

F3 I cannot settle. The rider did send "Sure, your call." at 18:43, before the 18:46 segment start, answering the 18:42 proposal to go round via Rifle Range Road, so the RD-5 timing is met [F9][F10][F11][F3]. But the scope is not readable: the only named road is Rifle Range Road, and no fact ties the driven 18:46–18:56 path (7.10 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.43 km, straying up to 1923 m) to that road, no stop was measured on it, and the driver's statement names no road for this segment either; "your call" can equally be read as a general routing choice, which would not cover a loop that is nothing of the driver's own but would cover the route chosen to get there [F9][F10][F12][F3][RD-5]. Under RD-5 that is undetermined (G13).

The undetermined scope of F3 changes the amount: if the consent is read as general, only F4 counts (4.78 km × $1.4100/km = $6.74); if F3 is treated as being off the consented road, F3 also counts (5.66 km × $1.4100/km = $7.98, total $14.72, the sum of the two segments' extra km; the rate is F5's distance fare ÷ distance km, $43.64 ÷ 30.95 = $1.40998/km, and the remainder of the $14.64 excess-distance line stays unrecovered) [F3][F4][F5][RD-2]. Because the record does not settle which reading applies, a person must decide; a machine applying either reading would risk under- or over-refunding [F3][RD-5].

No RD-6 flag arises: the trace marks the prior-upheld-route-dispute precondition ✗ (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 for this driver), and profile facts alone never decide or add an account action [F17][F18][RD-6]. The $0.11 meter waiting unit and the $1.47 platform fee are undisturbed in either reading [F6][F8][RD-3][FARE-1].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement; they concern congestion and routing only — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F12]. The escalation rests on the undetermined RD-5 scope of F3, not on safety.
